Three of the remaining items are fixable kernel fusions; this PR carries them. ## Split DFlash buffer padding into one wide launch `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` padded the drafter's CUDA-graph buffers inside every per-group launch, blocked at the BLOCK_SIZE derived from the per-request token span — 8 on a decode step — so the four pad regions cost thousands of serialized 8-wide stores, repeated once per draft KV cache group over shared output buffers. The trace shows 3 launches per step at 42.7-44.8 us each: 131 us of the 170.7 us eager GPU section, 77% of it. The padding now runs as its own launch with a fixed 256-wide block, called once from `propose()` before the per-group loop: one grid spans the qsl, seq_lens, sample and query pad regions (each indexes its own buffer from zero, so the grid covers the largest region end), and pads every draft group's row of the shared slot-mapping table through a cached group-id tensor. Buffer addresses and every written value are unchanged, so replay semantics and the existing `test_dflash_prepare_inputs` assertions hold. ## Build the native indexer decode lens in one kernel The native MTP branch of `_prepare_decode_tensors` built the `(B, max_decode_len)` per-token context lengths as a broadcast chain (sub, add, clamp) into the decode seq-lens view. That is three launches per indexer metadata build, and the profiled step ran the chain on each of its builds between graph replays. It is now one `PrepareNativeDecodeLensKernel` launch writing `max(seq_lens[b] - max_decode_len + j + 1, 0)` directly over a 256-wide block-strided grid (`cdiv(num_decodes * max_decode_len, 256)` programs, each covering a vector of rows), following the warmup-registered `PrepareUniformDecodeKernel` pattern (compile key over the max_decode_len specialization class, registered in the three attention backends that register its sibling). The now-unused `offsets_buffer` arange is removed. The compress-ratio divide stays a separate op: it must run after DCP localizes the decode seq lens, so folding it in would change floor-div semantics under sharding. ## Fuse the Gumbel sample finalize into one kernel `gumbel_sample` reduced its per-block partials with `local_max.argmax` followed by a gather of `local_argmax` — two kernels inside the captured decode graph, ~6 us per sampling round at three rounds per step. One finalize kernel now reduces the partial row and loads the winning token id in a single program, preserving torch.argmax's first-occurrence tie break via a where/min index select. This one saves in-graph GPU time only; it removes no host dispatch. ## Ruled out by the trace - The 301 us/step `nvjet` GEMM is the in-graph lm_head streaming ~1.85 GB of bf16 weights at tiny M — weight-bandwidth-bound, not a fusion item. - The engram hash/lookup chain is in-graph, with per-layer embedding tables prefetched on a side stream; batching the lookups would serialize work the prefetch currently overlaps. - The two paged-MQA metadata builds cannot merge: deep_gemm returns fresh tensors and the DtoD copies exist to keep CUDA-graph address stability. - Folding the image-sentinel mask polarity saves no launches: both polarities are consumed. ## End-to-end measurement Campaign dsv41-pd-fusions-e2e-fus-004-20261025-1430 on the PD deployment (2x8 H200, TP1 x DP8, MTP 3, aiperf CC-trace load, nyann, gsm8k), stacked on the same base as the four-PR run before it (`vllm-main` at `e9acf4861`; exp = `dsv41-decode-fusions` at `e39a4dcd`, i.e. this PR on top of #63523). The previous campaign (fus-003) is the four-PR stack, so the delta isolates this PR. - aiperf ITL p50: c8 4.93 -> 4.85 ms, c16 5.07 -> 4.98, c32 5.77 -> 5.72, c64 6.78 -> 6.70, c128 8.77 -> 8.66. ITL p90 came down at every stage as well. Request counts, ISL/OSL p50 and error counts match between the runs; output tok/s holds within +-0.8% at c16-c128. - nyann ITL p50 (ISL/OSL 2048): 15.5 -> 15.3, 18.2 -> 18.0, 23.0 -> 22.9 ms. - gsm8k flexible-extract 0.9697 +-0.0047 -> 0.9712 +-0.0046, strict-match 0.9689 -> 0.9682 (within stderr), 0 errors. Each individual latency number sits inside the +-2% band same-build repeats of this deployment span; the sign is uniform across all thirteen decode-latency measurements (aiperf p50 and p90 at five concurrencies, nyann p50 at three). The c16 saving, ~90 us/step, matches the trace's ~120 us eager-GPU estimate net of the new pad launch. The branch now sits above the measured build through commits carried in by the rebase and one local refinement: #63523's mypy narrowing fix and its upload-on-change params-table cache (no per-step copy), plus this PR's decode-lens kernel moving to a 256-wide block-strided grid in place of one program per token. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? +    Mirrors ``build_attn_metadata``: the query and seq-len tensors are shared
+    across groups, the token-to-request cache threads from group to group,
+    and each group has its own slot mapping and block table. The first token
+    is padded (slot -1) so the invalid-token path of the decode kernel runs.
